steps.title: Linux & Networking Fundamentals
steps.subtitle: Command the server and the network
steps.description: Get comfortable on the Linux command line, manage permissions, processes and systemd services, and learn how TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP and TLS move traffic between machines. Every server, container and pipeline you will run sits on this foundation, and interviewers probe it first.

topics.name: Linux shell and filesystem: navigation, find, grep, pipes and redirection
Users, groups and file permissions (chmod, chown, sudo, octal notation)
Processes, signals and services (ps, top, kill, systemctl, journalctl)
TCP/IP model, IP addressing, subnets and CIDR, ports, TCP vs UDP
DNS resolution, record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT) and TTL, using dig
HTTP methods and status codes, HTTPS and TLS certificates
SSH keys and network troubleshooting (ping, curl, ss, traceroute)

steps.title: Git, Scripting & CI/CD
steps.subtitle: Automate everything from commit to build
steps.description: Collaborate with Git, automate repetitive work with Bash and Python, and build CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions or Jenkins that test, package and ship every change. Automation is the heart of a DevOps role.

topics.name: Git fundamentals: commit, branch, merge, rebase, revert and resolving conflicts
Branching strategies and the pull-request workflow (feature branches, trunk-based, code review)
Bash scripting: variables, conditionals, loops, exit codes, set -euo pipefail and cron
Python for automation: files, subprocess, REST APIs, JSON and YAML
CI/CD concepts: continuous integration, delivery vs deployment, pipeline stages
Pipelines with GitHub Actions or Jenkins: triggers, jobs, runners and dependencies
Test and artifact stages, dependency caching and handling pipeline secrets

steps.title: Containers with Docker
steps.subtitle: Package apps to run the same everywhere
steps.description: Write efficient Dockerfiles, understand image layers and build caching, persist data with volumes, connect services with Docker Compose and publish small, secure images to a registry. Containers are the unit of deployment on every modern cloud platform.

topics.name: Containers vs virtual machines, images vs containers, and the container lifecycle
Writing Dockerfiles: FROM, RUN, COPY, CMD vs ENTRYPOINT and .dockerignore
Image layers, build cache ordering and multi-stage builds
Volumes, bind mounts, port publishing and Docker networks
Multi-container apps with Docker Compose (services, depends_on, healthchecks)
Registries, tags vs digests, and image security (minimal bases, non-root users, scanning)

steps.title: Cloud & Infrastructure as Code
steps.subtitle: Provision scalable, secure infrastructure
steps.description: Learn the core services of AWS (with their Azure and GCP equivalents): compute, storage, IAM and VPC networking, and design for high availability with load balancers and autoscaling. Then define it all in Terraform so environments are repeatable, reviewable and easy to rebuild.

topics.name: Cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), regions and availability zones
Core services: virtual machines (EC2), object storage (S3), block storage and managed databases
IAM users, roles and policies, least privilege and secrets managers
VPC networking: public and private subnets, route tables, internet and NAT gateways, security groups
High availability: load balancers, auto scaling groups and multi-AZ design
Terraform basics: providers, resources, variables, plan and apply
Terraform state, remote backends with locking, modules and immutable infrastructure

steps.title: Kubernetes, Observability & Reliability
steps.subtitle: Run, monitor and recover production systems
steps.description: Deploy and scale containers on Kubernetes with Deployments, Services, Ingress, probes and Helm, then keep them healthy with Prometheus and Grafana, centralised logging, SLO-based alerting, safe rollout strategies and calm incident response.

topics.name: Kubernetes architecture: control plane, nodes, kubelet and kubectl basics
Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, ConfigMaps and Secrets
Services (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer) and Ingress
Liveness and readiness probes, resource requests and limits, HPA and Helm charts
Metrics, logs and traces: Prometheus, Grafana dashboards, centralised logging and alerting
Deployment strategies: rolling, blue-green, canary and rollbacks
SLIs, SLOs and error budgets, incident response, postmortems and disaster recovery (RPO/RTO)
